head: d5659d24f6e5c332f1228425a0bef8d6396630b3
summary:
SL-104 changes only the settled rules in .taad/fitness.yaml (rule 2 now has 11 patterns, rule 4 has 7, plus one new Attributes entry under a single '# settled by SL-104' marker), 25 plant rows and the tests under tests/bugs. src is untouched. I re-ran everything against the real taad3 engine and this tree.
- The Fitness tool reports 92 rules on the real tree, every rule holds.
- harness --scenario all: 161/161 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits.
- The class corpus passes under pwsh and PS 5.1. Against the pre-slice yaml (824622e) it fails 90 checks, so the corpus catches the bug.
- rules-parity is AGREE with 70 settled entries in both shells. RuleCases C-001 passes. The xUnit rule tests pass 19/19.
- Independent check: I wrote 46 plant cases of my own (my own spellings, not the build's rows) and put each in Store, the Core root and a non-excepted Scanning file, then ran them through taad3.fitness.content_hits. Against the new yaml there were 0 failures: every fire case fired its rule in all 3 places and every quiet case was quiet for R2, R4 and RA. The same cases against the pre-slice yaml fired none of R2, R4 or RA.
- O-015 and O-016 are verified.
- One extra observation: the receiver-free `\.(Encrypt|Decrypt)\b` pattern also fires on a non-file call such as rsa.Encrypt(...). That over-fencing goes to the backlog. The object-initializer residual (item 14) still gets through, as the design says it will, and both because-texts name it.
Contact is graded `code`. A rule-text slice has no device to touch, and the engine ran on scratch copies of the tree.

criteria.criterion: 1. Fence the reported spellings: File.SetAttributes qualified and fully qualified, and DirectoryInfo GetFiles/GetDirectories with and without arguments (W01-W03, L01-L04), while W20, W21, L20 and L21 stay quiet
criteria.how: Engine's repro exit 0 (O-001). In my own engine matrix, A1-A3 fire R2 and A4-A7 fire R4 in all 3 places, while Q1-Q4 (the W20/W21/L20/L21 reads) get 0 R2/R4/RA hits. Against the pre-slice yaml the same lines fired none of R2, R4 or RA.

criteria.criterion: 2. File.SetAttributes in a file of its own under Store/, judged by the real engine
criteria.how: Harness S58 is AS-RECORDED. My B1 (global::System.IO.File.SetAttributes in its own file) and A1 fire R2 in Store/ through taad3.fitness.content_hits.

criteria.criterion: 3. Using static System.IO.File: bare SetAttributes(...) and SetLastWriteTimeUtc(...)
criteria.how: C1 SetAttributes(...), C2 SetLastWriteTimeUtc(...) and C3 'SetCreationTime (p, t)' with a space before the parenthesis all fire R2 in 3 places. Harness S59 and S60 are AS-RECORDED.

criteria.criterion: 4. IsReadOnly setter fires; 'IsReadOnly => false' and 'IsReadOnly == true' stay quiet
criteria.how: D1 'new FileInfo(path).IsReadOnly = true;' and D4 'fi.IsReadOnly=false;' fire R2. D2 '=> false', D3 '== true' and D5 (a plain read) are quiet in all 3 places. Harness S61, S73 and S81 are AS-RECORDED.

criteria.criterion: 5. ZwSetInformationFile and ZwQueryDirectoryFile as calls, and File.Encrypt
criteria.how: E1 fires R2 and E2 fires R4, both as calls. E3 File.Encrypt, E4 File.Decrypt and E5 fi.Decrypt() fire R2. In Store/ each fires only its own rule. Harness S62, S63, S69 and S82 are AS-RECORDED.

criteria.criterion: 6. DirectoryInfo GetFiles()/GetDirectories(...) directly under src/FsAnalyser.Core, in Store, and in a non-DirectoryReader Scanning file
criteria.how: A4-A7 fire R4 in Store/, at the Core root (**/ at zero levels) and in Scanning/ValPlant*.cs. Harness S64, S65 and S78 are AS-RECORDED.
G1 (dir.GetFiles;) and G2 (di.GetDirectories;) fire R4 in 3 places. Harness S66 is AS-RECORDED.

criteria.criterion: 14. Object initializer { Attributes = ..., LastWriteTime = ... } (non-material: listed so the next slice can disagree, expected to escape)
criteria.how: Z1 gets 0 hits from R2 and RA in all 3 places, the escape the design expected. Rule 2's and the Attributes entry's because-texts both name it as unseen by a text rule, and the corpus pins it as a residual row. Closing it is the filed-for-later symbol/AST decision.

obligations.evidence: Through the real engine (content_hits, 92 rules) the Store/ plants fired exactly one rule each. ZwSetInformationFile call, File.Encrypt, File.Decrypt and fi.Decrypt() fired {R2}. ZwQueryDirectoryFile call and using-static EnumerateFiles/EnumerateDirectories fired {R4}. No other rule fired. Harness rows S62, S63, S69 and S76 are AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits across all 161 rows.

Exactly one '# settled by SL-104' marker is in .taad/fitness.yaml, committed in d5659d2. The design's architecture_rules name 'Core sets no file attributes through a FileSystemInfo.Attributes write', files 'src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.cs', appears once in fitness.load(repo). design.py:1124-1137 skips names that are already loaded, so a re-run cannot append a second copy. The pattern in the block is the M1 one, edited in place per accepted M4. design-slice-1.json still carries the pre-M1 text, which is code review's recorded drift and is harmless while the block exists.

not_reached: The engine's merge/commit-time gate (minorlane) was not run. I ran fitness.check through the MCP tool and the harness, not the gate itself.
My planted lines were matched as text and never compiled. The build's corpus compiled its own spellings. That matters for a text rule only if a quiet row would not compile in real code.
I did not run the whole xUnit suite. src is unchanged, and only the yaml-reading rule tests were run.
I did not re-run RuleCases C-002..C-005. The build ran them one at a time and they passed. I re-ran C-001 and rules-parity.

These spellings stay unfenced and are carried on the backlog, not checked here: deconstruction assignment and ++/-- on Attributes (SC-321), method groups through a using alias (SC-322), whitespace, comment or @ between the dot and the member (SC-323), object initializers, reflection, and delegates from using-static method groups.
Nothing in the default `dotnet test` run enforces rules 2 and 4 or the Attributes entry, because they have no xUnit twin. Only the Fitness check and the harness do.
